about: What the sessions changed on the site, newest first, in plain words for the owner's Admin page ('What changed lately'). Add with: python3 check-tools/admin.py change "<what>". Nothing private: both repositories are public.

changes.what: On a phone the menu and the market panel no longer pop when let go: they glide on at the finger's speed and slow down gently, and the menu slides more smoothly on an iPhone

On a phone the menu and the market panel open without the dark shade behind them (iPhone Safari changed its shade as they settled, which looked like a flicker); the green market button no longer sits on top of the open menu

The 25 daily screener pages now have the market panel on the right (desktop) and the green button or a swipe on a phone, as a 4-week trial; their tables also fit a phone now. Not added to guides, legal or stock pages, to keep them uncluttered

Every page now has the same header: on a phone the guides, legal pages and daily screener pages get the menu button, bell, swipe and usage count; on a desktop the usage count and your name in the Account menu. The weekly phone check now tests every page's header

Stock pages with no news at all (49 of the 946 in Google, all outside the US, e.g. Ramsay Health Care) now take the newest article clearly about the company, even if it is not 'critical' news; from Monday's run

The stock pages showed Thursday's figures on Saturday (this morning's update had crashed before writing them): refreshed by hand to Friday's close and uploaded; the crash itself is fixed for Monday's run

Daily market pages: the headings over numbers are right-aligned; the hub's 'Scoring above zero' is now 'In a rising trend' with its percentage and a line explaining it, the columns line up across regions, and each leader is clickable
Home page: the intro's middle button is now Today's top 10s (the daily market pages, free for every visitor) in place of US Stock Screener, which stays in the menu

Shares without a stock page on the daily market pages now open and run their analysis (the link lacked one setting); the home page's link to every market's top 10 is a button at the top of its section; the Admin page's questions show the live ones first, answered ones folded as history
Every share on the daily market pages can be clicked: one without a stock page opens its full analysis; the Screeners menu on every page has a new entry, Today's top 10s

Home page: a new section near the top, This week in the markets: the big scheduled announcements coming up (in the visitor's own time) and how the trend stands across 24 markets today, rewritten every day

Practice portfolio: Show the figures (and every other fold) stays open when prices refresh; the figures list shows the latest 14 days (7 on a phone) with Show all; the graph opens on All after a page refresh

The autopilot now knows the market's calendar: big scheduled announcements (Fed, ECB, inflation, jobs) for the next two days and what came out in the last day go to its AI with the market's headlines when it chooses; they show in What happens next; every buy records how close it was to one and to its company's results; the month's OpenAI cost is on the Admin page
Practice portfolio graph: the 3m, 6m, 1y and longer buttons are hidden until the account is old enough, and pressing Your own buys or AI autopilot no longer moves the buttons or the graph
New public pages, one for each of 24 markets plus a hub: the day's top 10 by trend with why each ranks there, updated every day, for visitors from Google (stockiq.tech/screeners-today.html)

Fed decision days studied on five years of prices: no direction, only larger moves, so no rule; each company's results date is now kept so the autopilot can learn whether holding through results helps or hurts
The daily update's email says when it started, how long it took, and warns (⚠️) when a step failed inside a run that still finished
The daily update had stopped refreshing the stock pages' figures on 24 Oct (too many open files under the Mac's scheduler): the limit is raised, from the next run
The Improvements tab now opens with the story: the score against an S&P 500 fund, what testing has proven (with its figures), what is being tested for profit and how far along, and what is next
The Improvements tab opens with three plain lines: what it works on next, what the last session improved, and what is being tested
At least two of the three parts each session works on are now profit and growth areas, so most of each session goes where the money is
Every weekly session now also questions its own process: for each problem you had to point out, why no check caught it first, and that gap is closed too
The Improvements tab is tidied into six short rows (being tested, ideas, decided, fixes, questions, parts of the site), each with its count and the one thing worth knowing; open a row for the detail

The weekly review now asks why every trade ended as it did (its whole market, one event, or the share itself) and sets each against its own market; the first answer: most losses were single shares, and the picks are not yet clearly better than their markets. Next: record the news at each sale
Refined: a look at a profit or growth part of the site must always end in an improvement; other parts may end 'fine as it is' with the reason, and then wait until they change
Every look at a part of the site must now end in an improvement (fixed, improved, simplified, a new idea to test, or a new question): 'it's fine' is not accepted

Parts of the site are no longer just rotated: next come those never looked at, then those whose code changed since their last look, profit-related ones sooner; each look starts from what was found before, and an unchanged part waits

The list of site parts reviewed in turn is complete: 58 parts, now including the path from first visit to sign-up and paying, speed, security, every email and the checks themselves; every page and script must belong to a part, checked at every session

Admin page: each check now says what it covers (Full check: every test on the live site; Page scan: links, descriptions, stale pages); the Improvements tab lists every part of the site with when it was looked at and what was found; two new profit ideas
The Improvements tab's number now means 'being tested'; the tab starts with links to each section (being tested, ideas, done, fixes, the 48 questions)
Cost check: today's changes add nothing noticeable; found and fixed one cost (a large record rewritten every 30 minutes, about 5c a month). StockIQ runs at about 85c a month

The Improvements tab now lists every fix and change with who found the problem behind it, and counts how many you pointed out: the checks should find them first. Two more automatic checks: every 'Needs you' warning is verified at each session, and the weekly check times how fast your prices load
Fixed a false 'Needs you' warning (it left the sector funds out of its sums); the screeners the AI chooses are greyed out and locked again, with a clearer tick
Clearer ticks for the screeners the AI chooses; the autopilot emails only when something changes how it trades (not its daily notes); prices update as soon as you return to the Practice portfolio

The number of holdings and the budget are now automatic: 42 holdings (about 2 for each screener ticked, each from the top 10 of its list) and all the practice money it can reach. The improvement lists are checked against what is live at every session
The Improvements tab now also lists every question asked about making it better (46), with what was found, so an idea already tried is not tried again; three missing entries added
The Practice portfolio's prices load in about 3 seconds instead of about 15: they are asked for six requests at a time instead of one request per holding
Practice portfolio: click any holding or sold line (the name with 🔍) to run its full analysis in the background; it lands in your Reports

Practice portfolio: the All markets row of the market list now shows the totals (total bought, result, against the S&P 500); the graph has 1d to 10y; 'Account' is 'All markets'; the list no longer jumps to the top

Admin page: each decision shows when it was raised and Claude's recommended answer; 'Coming up' is one line a day with the real-money date apart; the 'so far' and forecast lines say plainly what each means. The unsubscribe page now really unsubscribes

New: 'Who chooses the markets' on the AI autopilot's Settings: AI (the boxes are greyed out and the autopilot keeps the main index of every country, leaving a market out only while its own trades lag) or Manual. Settings is also much shorter

The crypto screener no longer gives extra points to a coin that has just jumped (on its own record such coins fell back 12% on average); the 'check-in has not happened' warning no longer fires on a market holiday; the Improvements list is newest first, every line dated
Admin page: 'So far' (the record) and 'Claude's forecast' are now clearly two different things; the so-far reading had a fault (it left out the first and latest days) and leaned the wrong way
Small charts in the market panel now always match the colour of the change beside them

Weekly check done early: 50 of 54 passed (the 4 are fixed and waiting to go live). Two new trials for the autopilot: wait one check-in after an overnight fall through the loss limit, and test whether the AI model's picks beat simply taking the top-ranked share
The Practice portfolio's prices now refresh by themselves every minute while you're on the tab (the button stays)
Took the old boast off the bottom of every page ('Professional Investment Research Platform', 'Powered by AI') and three similar lines; the nightly check now catches such wording
The AI autopilot's breakdown now starts with shares against coins, and every line shows the dollars made or lost
On this page: 'Coming up' under the check-in answer (your next check-in, the next full check and review, decisions, the goal), and a row 'What runs by itself' with when each last ran
The Admin page is calmer: your two questions first (do you need to check in; real money with the confidence dial and the month's goal), then what changed, and the rest as rows you open
At the top of this page: Real money, the decision. One verdict from four checks, decided on 11 Oct 2027; until then it shows how each check stands
The confidence line on this page is now a dial: red under 50%, yellow to 90%, green from 90%, with a line of how it has moved day by day (faded until 30 trading days)
On the AI autopilot's Activity part, the themes part, the bar, progress and how it improves are each a row that opens and closes where it is
Under the month's goal on this page: how sure the record is that the account has been ahead of an S&P 500 fund so far (too early to tell until 30 trading days)

The autopilot's holdings are listed once, on the Practice portfolio tab, each with its tags (market closed until…, its stop, patient share) and a 'Can be sold now' choice; the autopilot tab links there instead of listing them again

Month targets raised above break-even; the home page's first sentence is clearer and its stock links sit compactly at the bottom; market panel clicks run the analysis (in the background on the dashboard)
The autopilot's budget now grows with the profit of its sales and shrinks with its losses (a tick box under the budget, on by default), always within the practice money there is
A holding's trailing stop is now watched every half hour between check-ins, so a gain is not handed back while waiting up to 3 hours for the next check-in
Stock pages' news shows the right dates again (6,931 wrong date stamps corrected), and about 600 unchanged pages a day are no longer re-uploaded
On a phone the dashboard's market-data button is no longer hidden under the AI chat button, and the chat window fits small screens
